title: How do you like to learn?
intro: Twenty quick either/or questions. There are no right answers; pick the option closer to you. AdaptAid uses your answers as a starting point and adjusts as it sees what actually works for you.
note: Written for AdaptAid on the four Felder–Silverman dimensions. It is not the official Index of Learning Styles; students who have taken the ILS can enter their scores instead.

items.prompt: When I learn a new algorithm, I'd rather…
items.a: try coding it straight away
items.b: read it through and think about how it works first

items.prompt: In a study group I usually…
items.a: listen and think before I say anything
items.b: jump in and try ideas out loud

items.prompt: When I get stuck on a problem, I tend to…
items.a: try different things until something works
items.b: stop and think it through carefully

items.prompt: I remember things better when I…
items.a: have thought them over on my own
items.b: have done something with them

items.prompt: Practice exercises are most useful to me…
items.a: as soon as I've seen the idea once
items.b: after I understand the theory well

items.prompt: I prefer explanations that…
items.a: start from a concrete example
items.b: start from the general principle

items.prompt: I find it more interesting to learn…
items.a: the theory of why something works
items.b: how to use it to solve real problems

items.prompt: When I read a proof or derivation, I…
items.a: check each step carefully against an example
items.b: look for the key insight

items.prompt: I would describe myself as more…
items.a: imaginative
items.b: practical

items.prompt: With a new topic I like to…
items.a: learn the standard method and practise it
items.b: find my own way of approaching it

items.prompt: When I think about a linked list, I mostly…
items.a: picture boxes and arrows
items.b: think of a description in words

items.prompt: I learn more from…
items.a: a clear written explanation
items.b: a diagram or animation

items.prompt: Someone gives me directions. I'd rather have…
items.a: a map
items.b: written step-by-step instructions

items.prompt: After a lecture I remember best…
items.a: what was said or written
items.b: the pictures and diagrams

items.prompt: When I explain an idea to a friend, I…
items.a: sketch it
items.b: talk them through it

items.prompt: When I study a new chapter, I…
items.a: go through it section by section, in order
items.b: skim it first to see the whole picture

items.prompt: I understand a topic best when…
items.a: I see how it fits with everything else
items.b: I master each step before moving on

items.prompt: When solving a problem, I usually…
items.a: work forward one step at a time
items.b: see the answer suddenly, then fill in the steps

items.prompt: A good course outline for me…
items.a: shows the big picture and connections up front
items.b: lists the topics in a clear order

items.prompt: If I miss one step in an explanation, I…
items.a: find it hard to follow the rest
items.b: can usually still get the overall idea
